data_quality_notes:
Research ran 06:33-07:40 ET and logged a RESEARCH COMPLETE block, so this report is a full synthesis rather than a salvage. All 15 unique candidates captured were re-checked here: reward-to-risk was recomputed from entry, target, and stop (bear-case price for long-term) without reference to the figure in the notes, and all 15 cleared their floors independently. Nothing was dropped and nothing was added. Prices were refreshed at 07:02 ET and every quote returned the 2026-08-17 close, since the cash session has not opened; last_price is therefore prior close throughout, not a live tick.

Flags the reader should weigh before sizing:
(1) DIRECTIONAL SKEW — 14 long, 1 short, into a tape with index futures down 0.4-1.1% pre-open. Research attempted an index-futures hedge (short /MNQU6) and rejected it because the honest arithmetic gave 1.82 against a 2.0 floor. The skew is disclosed, not corrected. Treat the book as long-biased and size accordingly.
(2) REWARD-TO-RISK CLUSTERING — eight of fifteen sit within 0.25 of their floor (BABA 2.08, MGPI 2.10, /MCLV6 2.13, TJX 2.15, HD 2.17, BCC 2.20, PFE 2.54, CCJ 2.61). This repo has previously shipped ratios nudged to clear a bar, so this pattern deserves suspicion on its face. In each case the downside level traces to a named structural feature — a stacked sma50/sma200, a prior range low, a dividend-cut valuation — rather than being back-solved from the target, but the clustering is real and these eight warrant the red team's first look.
(3) NO INTRADAY IDEAS. The only same-day catalyst was HD's 6:00am print, and no premarket price was obtainable, so HD is published as a swing with an explicit hold-above-sma50 trigger rather than with invented intraday levels.
(4) NO EVENT CONTRACTS. market_data.py events returned count=0 for nine topic queries (CPI, inflation, recession, government, S&P, Bitcoin, oil price, Nasdaq, Powell); the tenth returned four irrelevant tennis markets with null prices. The lane is empty because nothing was fetchable, not because nothing was looked for. No probability was invented.
(5) MHO insiders sold $14.2M across 30 transactions with zero buys — a homebuilder-insider caution flag sitting directly against the HD/BCC/LOW housing cluster.

Coverage gaps: no live VIX, DXY or index spot for the entire run (yahoo returned HTTP 429 on ^GSPC, ^NDX, ^DJI, ^RUT, ^VIX, ES=F, NQ=F, DX=F, GC=F, CL=F), so ETF proxies are used throughout and those market_context levels are null. Gold was dropped entirely: no verified spot price was obtainable and two written sources disagreed by roughly $400/oz, so no level would have been defensible. HD's premarket reaction was unobtainable. PATK's Form 425 could not be read from EDGAR directly (403); merger terms came from stocktitan filing summaries cross-checked against the company IR page.

Other failed sources: alphavantage (no API key), stooq (404 on index symbols), finnhub index quotes (paid CFD subscription), kalshi events search, whitecase.com (403, substituted wiley.law for equivalent legal content), cmegroup.com contract calendar (60s timeout; the WTI expiry was derived from the published CME rule and cross-checked against the fetched Sep/Oct strip), and market_data.py quote returned no data for PCH and SUM. Equity and ETF quotes via finnhub worked all run.

Count: fifteen ideas is what cleared the bar, not a target. Six are position management on the nine open positions (XLE, KRE, TJX, CCJ, NKE, and the BTC instrument correction) rather than new risk. Total sizing is 38% of trading capital. Driver concentration sits at the strategy cap of 3 on two clusters: Hormuz/crude (/MCLV6, XLE, DHT) and housing repair-and-remodel (HD, BCC, LOW). LCII carries a partial housing overlap that is disclosed rather than netted out — housing is 31% of pro forma Patrick revenue — but its driver is the merger and the outdoor-recreation cycle.

RED TEAM (phase 2c, separate pass, adversarial). Cut four of fifteen; eleven survive.

DHT's dated catalyst was removed: the Aug 24 date was a dividend payment on a stock that went ex on Aug 17 and moves nothing, so this trade correctly has no near-term dated catalyst (this also resolves the validator's earnings-calendar warning). PFE's three insider buys were re-verified against the Form 4s themselves rather than the news write-up and are exact to the dollar ($2.96M, all code P), so the primary filings are now the leading sources; its 6.9% yield claim was corrected to 6.4% at 26.87. NOT CUT, and stated rather than implied: the directional skew is worse after this pass, not better — ten long and one short. Total sizing falls from 38% to 29.0% of trading capital. market_context.summary: Two drivers own the tape. First, the Strait of Hormuz: commodity vessel transits collapsed to five on Sat Aug 15 and zero on Sun Aug 16 against 31 the prior weekend after tanker attacks, with VLCC Middle East-Asia spot rates near $500,000/day against a $20,000-60,000 baseline. Yet Brent at 90.97 sits about $14 below its 105 print of Jul 23, when the physical situation was materially better — the market is pricing headlines, not observed flow interruption. Note the internal divergence: USO +2.91% against SLB +0.17%, so the bid is in the barrel rather than in the service names. Second, the first-ever use of Section 338: 50% duties on roughly $20B of targeted Canadian goods — plywood, furniture, cement, whisky, dairy explicitly named, with no USMCA exemption — take effect 12:01am ET Wed Aug 19, the same morning TJX, LOW and TGT report. Motor vehicles are the stated grievance but are NOT on the covered list. Underneath both, the 10-year rose to 4.68% while the 10s2s curve steepened to +0.53 and unemployment fell to 4.1%: a growth and term-premium steepener rather than a recession steepener, which supports hard assets and bank margin while pressuring long-duration equity. Index futures were down 0.4-1.1% pre-open on the combination of higher yields and higher oil.

If Hormuz actually closes rather than merely becoming expensive, DHT tonnage stops earning altogether, and one missile hitting a DHT hull is a permanent loss of a vessel with only 3-10%-of-hull war-risk cover that the company is now paying for. War risk premiums at 3-10% of hull value also consume a meaningful share of the headline rate.
recommendations.counter_argument: This is a cyclical at the top of the cycle by every conventional measure — 76.7% above its 250-day low, above its sma20, sma50 and sma200, on rates roughly 10x normal that no one argues are sustainable. Tanker equities historically peak when spot rates peak, not when earnings print, so the record Q2 and the coming record Q3 may both arrive after the stock has topped. A ceasefire headline removes the entire thesis in one session.

recommendations.thesis: Update to the 2026-08-17 long: a continuing multi-year accumulation, and explicitly not an add at today's price. Cameco has contracted average annual deliveries of over 28 million pounds for the next five years against production guidance of 19.5-21.5 million pounds, written with floors in the high $70s and ceilings near $160 escalated, so realized price rises mechanically as the term price moves from the mid-$90s into three digits. Management stated they have never been at this kind of uranium price at the front end of a contracting cycle — the earnings power is contracted, not hoped for.
recommendations.key_risk: INVALIDATION, not a price move: the thesis is wrong if utility long-term contracting volumes fail to accelerate over the next two to three quarters, or if annual production guidance is cut below 19.5 million pounds on a sustained operational failure at Cigar Lake or McArthur River. The contract ceilings near 160 also cap the upside that the bull case depends on, and the 250-day low of 68.96 shows how far it can go without anything fundamental changing. Red team downgraded this from conviction 4 to 3 and cut size from 4% to 3%. The idea's own key_risk names the confirming indicator — utility long-term contracting volumes accelerating — and then states it 'has not yet turned', with management calling contracting only moderate. A thesis whose stated trigger has explicitly not fired is not a 4, and 4% sizing on an entry 10.7% below the market overstates a position that will most likely not transact this week.

catalyst.event: The post-de-rating earnings recovery: consensus has FY26 adjusted EPS bottoming at $1.67, down 23.6%, then rising 55.8% to $2.57 in FY27 as the wholesale rebuild under CEO Elliott Hill annualises
catalyst.action: accumulate in thirds — first below 40, second below 38, third below 35. There is no reason to rush a multi-year build into a stock making new lows; let it come to you.

recommendations.thesis: Update to the 2026-08-17 long: a continuing multi-year accumulation, with the next tranches deliberately lower rather than here. At 39.09 Nike trades at 15.2 times the $2.57 FY27 consensus, a multiple normally attached to a structurally impaired retailer rather than to the largest athletic brand in the world, and the $62 target is simply that FY27 number at 24 times. Four insiders including CEO Elliott Hill and Tim Cook bought $3.73M of stock in the open market in April with zero offsetting conviction sales — the people running the turnaround were buyers of it.
recommendations.key_risk: INVALIDATION, not a price move: the thesis is wrong if FY27 revenue fails to grow year over year, or if gross margin stays below 40% for two consecutive quarters, or if the wholesale rebuild stalls in North America — the segment that broke first. The stock closed at a fresh 12-year low of 39.09 on 2.4x normal volume, and there is no support level beneath it because the last time it traded here was 2014.
recommendations.counter_argument: Every one of those insider purchases was made at $42.27-43.34 in April and every one is now 8-11% underwater, so the insider signal has already been tested by the market and found early. The Aug 17 decline came from a competitor guiding revenue down, which is read-across evidence that the category, not just Nike, is deteriorating — and a category problem does not respond to a turnaround plan. Analyst dispersion from $23.35 to $126 is an admission that nobody can value this.

Bitcoin has fallen from above $93,000 at the start of 2026 to $64,098 and sits beneath its 20-day and 50-day EMAs after failing at $66,500, so the medium-term downtrend is intact and unbroken. Rising long-end yields are the specific mechanism against it — a 4.68% risk-free rate raises the hurdle on a zero-cashflow asset at the same moment the equity risk appetite that funds crypto is being withdrawn.
recommendations.key_risk: The 66,600 stop is only 3.9% above entry on an asset that routinely moves 5% in a session and trades through the weekend when equity hedges cannot be adjusted. A short squeeze from the crowded-long liquidation the analysts describe cuts both ways once the longs are actually gone.
recommendations.counter_argument: Bitcoin rose 1.12% in the last 24 hours while equity futures fell, which is the opposite of the risk-off correlation the thesis assumes. The 62,300-63,000 support zone has held repeatedly, base-case August targets cluster at $65,500 with bullish cases near $67,000, and a Middle East escalation that lifts oil has historically also bid Bitcoin as a debasement hedge — the same trade as being long gold and long crude.

catalyst.event: 50% Section 338 duty on Canadian plywood takes effect 12:01am ET Aug 19, 2026, with no USMCA exemption — plywood is explicitly on the covered list and Canada is the largest supplier of softwood veneer to the US
catalyst.action: enter into the Aug 18 weakness ahead of the 12:01am effective time; do not chase above 82.5

recommendations.thesis: The pass-through mechanism is already demonstrated rather than assumed: on its Q2 2026 call Boise Cascade attributed improving plywood pricing directly to reduced imports, printing $393 per thousand square feet, up 15% year over year, as Brazilian imports fell 25%. Removing the largest Canadian veneer supply at a 50% duty applies the same lever again, and BCC is the only name in the beneficiary screen trading above both its sma50 and sma200, which sit stacked at 76.9 and 76.4 and define the stop.
recommendations.key_risk: Plywood demand is housing demand, and the 10-year yield rose to 4.68% on Aug 14 from 4.63%. A tariff that tightens supply into a mortgage rate that is killing starts raises price and kills volume at the same time, which is margin-neutral at best. BCC also fell 1.56% on Aug 17 with the rest of building products. RED TEAM — scope risk this idea does not name: the same Section 338 action is described elsewhere in this report (see the MGPI entry, now cut) as one where trade press reports USMCA-compliant Canadian goods remain exempt, contradicting the law-firm alerts cited here. Canadian plywood is overwhelmingly USMCA-compliant, so 'no USMCA exemption' is an assertion from a secondary source on a question this report has itself shown to be live and unresolved. The independent leg — demonstrated pass-through as Brazilian imports fell 25% — survives that doubt; the dated catalyst does not. Size cut from 2.5% to 1.5% accordingly.
recommendations.counter_argument: BCC pleaded guilty to a Lacey Act felony in Q2 2026 with a $6.4M fine and five years probation, specifically over illegally imported plywood — a company on federal probation for import violations is an awkward vehicle for an import-restriction trade and faces compliance cost and headline risk. Insiders sold twice in six months and bought nothing.
